report.answer_text:
Lando Norris of McLaren won the 2025 Formula 1 World Drivers' Championship. It was very close.
The margin: Max Verstappen finished two points behind Norris in the final standings, 423 to 421.[1] Oscar Piastri, Norris's McLaren teammate, finished third, 13 points behind him.[2] That makes it a 2-point gap to Verstappen and 13 to Piastri.
The finale: The title went to the last race in Abu Dhabi with three drivers still in contention. It was the first title-deciding final round with more than two contenders since 2010.[3] Norris went in with a 12-point lead, and Verstappen was a further four points ahead of Piastri.[4] Verstappen won the race from pole, and Piastri, who passed Norris early on, finished second.[4] Norris's third place was enough. He needed only a top-three finish.[5]
Significance:
Norris ended Verstappen's four-year reign as champion. Verstappen had made an extraordinary late-season comeback but fell two points short.[6]
Norris became Britain's 11th F1 world champion and the first McLaren driver to win the title since Lewis Hamilton in 2008.[6]
